tagline.text: A pilgrimage farm where a white heaven awaits at the top of 456 steps

children.text: A hillside farm in San Joaquin, at Iloilo's southern tip, turned into a pilgrimage site: 456 steps pass biblical scene sculptures on the way up to a massive Divine Mercy cross and a snow-white "heaven" area at the summit. It's a great day trip combined with the farm experience and the nearby World Heritage Miagao Church and San Joaquin Church.
Garin Farm is a farm-and-pilgrimage resort in San Joaquin, the southernmost town in Iloilo province. It sits about
55km

southwest of Iloilo City, on about 15 hectares of hills and rice fields overlooking Panay Gulf. It began as a family-run farm, but after a pilgrimage trail tracing the biblical story and a giant cross were built on the hill, it became southern Iloilo's leading faith-based attraction and a favorite family outing spot.

Garin Farm's centerpiece is "Pilgrimage Hill." Climbing the 456 steps from the base to the summit, you pass life-size sculptures depicting biblical scenes in sequence — Jesus's birth and public ministry, the Last Supper, and the Way of the Cross. At the top stands a Divine Mercy cross about

(101 feet) tall, and beside it spreads a "heaven" area decorated with white steps, angel sculptures, and snow-white structures. Visitors never stop coming to photograph the all-white space against the blue sky and sea.

At the foot of the hill, the farm area brings together rice paddies, vegetable plots, a space to see livestock and small animals, an artificial lake and swimming pool, and restaurants and lodging, so even non-religious travelers can enjoy a relaxed half-day here. For Filipinos, it's a beloved pilgrimage site visited with family during Holy Week and holidays, while for foreign travelers, it's a place to feel firsthand how deeply Filipino Catholic faith runs through daily life.

Rather than visiting only Garin Farm, it's worth combining it into a "southern Iloilo church pilgrimage" route with the nearby UNESCO World Heritage Miagao Church, San Joaquin Church with its carved battle scene, and the Baroque Campo Santo cemetery, all a short drive away. It suits travelers interested in history, architecture, and religious culture, as well as families traveling with kids.
Climbing slowly to the summit, passing each biblical scene sculpture along the way, takes about
30 minutes–1 hour
. Rest stops along the way let children and elderly visitors climb at their own pace.
A massive cross about 31m tall standing atop the hill, visible even from the San Joaquin coast far below. Many pilgrims pray or light a candle beneath it.
An area near the summit decorated entirely with white steps and sculptures, the photo spot that made Garin Farm famous. Wearing white or brightly colored clothing makes for better photos.

blocks.title: Enjoying the view from the summit

children.text: From the summit, San Joaquin town and green rice fields spread out below, with Panay Gulf beyond, and on a clear day, the sea toward Guimaras and Negros stretches out in the distance. The view is especially good in the late afternoon as the sun goes down.

At the farm below the hill, you can see rice paddies, vegetable plots, livestock, and birds up close. It's a great way to show kids a Filipino countryside farm, and you can also play in the water at the artificial lake and swimming pool.
A coral-stone church in San Joaquin town, completed in
. It's designated a National Cultural Treasure for its distinctive facade, whose pediment is carved with a scene from the Battle of Tetuán, where Spanish forces defeated Moroccan troops.
A Spanish-era cemetery established in
, with a Baroque funerary chapel standing at the top of a stone staircase. It's right along the coastal road through San Joaquin town, making it an easy stop.

blocks.title: The artificial lake and water play

children.text: After coming down the hill, you can cool off at the farm's artificial lake and swimming pool. Many local families rest in the shaded gazebos by the lake and eat a packed lunch, and kids can spend the afternoon at the water play areas. Check on-site for fees and whether facilities are open.

wet season, afternoon showers are frequent and the steps get slippery, and when a typhoon comes, the facility sometimes closes.

Holy Week (the week before Easter) is the busiest time, packed with pilgrims walking the Way of the Cross, and Christmas, the year-end holidays, and weekends also bring many family visitors. For a quiet visit, early morning on a weekday is best. San Joaquin is also known for holding Pasungay, a traditional bull-fighting event, during its town festival, so check local notices for the festival schedule.

Most travelers stay in Iloilo City and visit as a day trip. If you want a quiet countryside night, you can stay in a resort room inside Garin Farm (about

per night) or a simple beach resort on the San Joaquin coast. A farm stay is convenient for anyone planning to climb the pilgrimage hill early in the morning, and you should book early for Holy Week and holidays.

The restaurant on the farm serves Filipino home cooking made with vegetables, chicken, and pork raised on the farm. Being a southern Iloilo coastal town, fresh grilled fish, vinegar-cured kilawin, and tangy sinigang soup are also common. Back in Iloilo City, round off your day with the local noodle dish La Paz batchoy and charcoal-grilled chicken inasal. Coconut sweets and rice cakes can be bought cheaply as snacks at the markets in Miagao and San Joaquin.
The pilgrimage hill is a place of worship. Avoid sleeveless tops or overly short clothing, and wear comfortable sneakers.
The "heaven" area at the summit is all white, so sunlight reflects strongly. Bring sunglasses, a hat, and sunscreen.
There aren't many places selling water along the steps, so bring a water bottle with you as you climb.
Admission fees, operating hours, and per-facility extra charges change often. Check the official page or call ahead for the latest information before visiting.
Miagao Church, San Joaquin Church, and Campo Santo are all on the same southern coastal road, so you can visit them along a single bus route.
Return buses become infrequent after dark. If you're planning to go back to Iloilo City, catch a bus no later than
If chartering a vehicle, allow plenty of time and agree on the route and waiting time with the driver in advance.

During Holy Week, there's a custom called Visita Iglesia, visiting several churches in turn to pray. If visiting during this period, walking the pilgrimage route linking Miagao and San Joaquin churches with Garin Farm alongside locals can be a special experience.
It's 456 steps to the area with the Divine Mercy cross and about 480 steps to the very top. If the steps are too much, you can take a golf cart (about
) to the pavilion or near the cross.

Climbing the steps at midday carries a significant risk of dehydration and heatstroke. If you have weak knees or heart disease, climb slowly with breaks, and rest in the shade immediately if you feel dizzy.
After rain, the steps and white flooring get slippery. Avoid sandals with slick soles.
Don't climb onto or lean against the sculptures for photos. Treating religious statues playfully is deeply disrespectful to locals.
Stay quiet in front of pilgrims who are praying, and don't photograph their faces.
In the animal area, don't feed the animals without permission, and watch that children don't reach inside the fences.
During Holy Week and holidays, crowds cause delays at entry and parking. Arrive early.
